acceptance: The skip reason states the current, true cause; or, if the bundled DuckDB runs the catalog's MERGE INTO statements correctly, the skip is removed and those operations run and validate
The decision is checked against the DuckDB version the project actually pins or resolves, with the version named in the PR
Tests covering the execution filter pass
context:
Found while re-measuring the SCD2 scale table for benchbox-site draft drafts/platform-deep-dives/drafts/apply-changes-into-vs-standard-sql.md (site PR #115), which now says the skip is a catalog decision rather than an engine limit.

2026-11-07: Done in PR #4073 (merge b50a9ac1bd). uv.lock resolves duckdb 1.5.5 (pyproject requires >=1.5.0,<2.0.0). With the skip bypassed, `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark write_primitives` at SF0.01 ran all 112 operations successfully with none skipped; the 21 rule-matched MERGE INTO operations (20 in the merge category plus bulk_load_upsert_mode) ran and validated. The skip module duckdb_write_primitives.py, its hook in core/write_primitives/benchmark.py and its gate test were removed, tests that expected the skip now assert the merge operations run, and changelog.d/fix-duckdb-merge-skip-reason.json was added. Noticed: medium-tier shard 2 stalled about 25 minutes at 98% on this PR and on unrelated PR #4076; the hanging test is unidentified.
description: DUCKDB_WRITE_PRIMITIVES_MERGE_SKIP_REASON in benchbox/sql_compat/rules/execution_filter/duckdb_write_primitives.py says 'DuckDB 1.3.2 rejects the catalog's MERGE INTO statements; keep them explicit skips until the bundled driver supports MERGE.' On DuckDB 1.5.5, the version uv resolved on 2026-11-02 at core 6f5692490e, a plain MERGE INTO succeeds. The skip still applies to every MERGE INTO operation, so the reason now gives a false cause for a catalog decision.
